Translate paradigm events into backend-neutral rendering dictionaries

Source: R/scripting.R
render_events.Rd

A fixation, text or mask event's trigger and a region-by-region event's critical_region_trigger (rendered as crit_trigger) must be the token "condition" or "item", rendered as "@condition_trigger" or "@item_trigger", or a whole number from 1 to 255, written as a number or as a string of digits and rendered as an integer. Any other value is refused, naming the event by its place in events, counted from 1.

Usage

render_events(events, timing, hz = 60)

Arguments

events

The design's event list, as resolve_events() returns it.

timing

The design's timing block, a named list. NULL or an empty list overrides nothing.

hz

The refresh rate, in Hz, at which *_frames durations are converted to milliseconds. The exporters pass the schema's presentation.assumed_refresh_hz, 60 when it is absent.

Value

A list of rendered events, one per event of events, except that a response collected from the onset of the text event before it is merged into that event as its respond entry.

Details

timing sets durations by event type, in place of an event's own duration_ms or duration_frames but not of a duration: block: fixation_ms or fixation_frames every fixation, word_ms or word_frames every text event whose trigger is "condition" and isi_ms or isi_frames every blank. Any other timing key is refused. So is a duration that is not a finite number of at least 0, whether a timing value or an event's own duration_ms or duration_frames where it is used.

Other design errors refused here include an unknown event type, a feedback event with no response or question event before it, case on an event that is not a text event and length_of on one that is not a mask. A response is refused when its from is other than onset or offset, or when it is collected from the onset of an event that is not a text event or that runs in other blocks.

A fixed duration is emitted as whole milliseconds (ms), the unit every backend consumes: OpenSesame and jsPsych schedule it directly, and the PsychoPy script converts it back into whole flips against the refresh rate it measures at start-up. A duration read from the items or jittered (a duration: block) is emitted as ms_column, the loop-table column holding each trial's milliseconds. A response or question event's timeout is in seconds, rounded to three places.

A response collected from the onset of the text event before it (see .response_from()) is rendered with that event, as its respond entry (keys and timeout). The text keeps its ms (or ms_column) as its longest display time, and the window runs from its onset for ms plus the timeout, so the total window is the one the two events had. A response collected from the offset stays an event of its own. Keys are rendered as lists, which jsonlite writes as arrays even for one key.

A text event's case is carried as it is, for the runners to apply. A mask's length_of is carried too, with the one character to repeat as its text, and the exporters write the mask out for their trials (see .sized_masks()).
